seen.extent: image 35 (876_037): 8 lines of signs under a longhand hymn; image 44 (876_046): 4 lines of signs set as the words under four staves of music; 2-4 sign groups at the end of about ten hymns (e.g. images 26, 31, 32, 33, 36, 38, 39)
seen.cipher: The signs are stenographic outlines, not cipher letters: joined geometric strokes, hooks, loops and detached vowel dots, one outline per word (6-9 outlines per verse line, spaced as words under the notes on image 44), and the last word on image 44 is finished in longhand ('savior'). The end-of-hymn marks are 2-4 such outlines where other hymns carry a longhand author name. No longhand transcription is written beside the two hymns.

1443.closed: Shorthand, seen on the leaves: images 35 and 44 of Winterthur ASC 876 show two hymn texts in stenographic word outlines (joined strokes, loops, vowel dots, one outline per word; last word of image 44 completed in longhand 'savior'), and the 'code' signatures are the same shorthand. The catalogue's 'code' is shorthand, unread but not a cipher.

seen.where: vestigia.hu (answers curl from the cloud, 11 Nov): https://www.vestigia.hu/documents/2807 (DF 295774, ASMi Sforzesco, Ungheria, sc. 645 no. 22), /documents/2808 (DF 295775, no. 23) and /documents/2809 (DF 295776, no. 24); the web_url page images of all three downloaded to scratch, contact sheets and 1500 px crops of 2807 p. 1 and 2809 p. 1 read
seen.extent: DF 295774: 2 written pages (recto about 45 lines, verso 26), about two thirds cipher; DF 295775: 4 written pages, mixed clear and cipher; DF 295776: 1 page of about 40 lines, most of it cipher, plus a 3-line ciphered address on the back
seen.cipher: One hand and one system on all three: runs of digits (3 4 5 8 9 0), Latin letters (y w g p q n m z) and a few signs (a crossed circle, #, a triple stroke, Greek-like ε), written continuously without word breaks and alternating with clear Italian (DF 295774 opens 'Nuperrime qua son stati rotti quelli bohemi del serenissimo quondam re Matthia'; DF 295776 has 'Vegno a Milano cum mancho de ducati sei' in clear). No decipherment is written between the lines or in the margins of any page; only later archivists' dates (1491?, 1492, '1491. 18. 8bris Buda').

seen.extent: Usteri p. 15 lists the same folios as the lead: second cipher in E II 399 fol. 128, 250, 287, 307, 360 and E II 400 fol. 8, 46, 76, 103, 122, 126, 278, 287, 295, 300, 305, 312, 329, 335, 337, 348; first cipher only in E II 399 fol. 105, 130, 137
seen.cipher: Per Usteri p. 15: two systems, one of letters only (four-letter groups with a shift by position), one of 'Buchstaben, Zeichen und Zahlen' with nulls (b d f h k m n p r t w y) and a nomenclator of nine three-digit numbers between points ('.235.' = Oxenstierna); Latin plaintext, mostly Peblis to Breitinger, 'der meist, aber nicht immer, die Aufloesung in Klarschrift an den Rand oder auf ein besonderes Blatt geschrieben hat'

prior_art.decode: not searched on de-crypt.org: settled by the printed study
prior_art.edition: Usteri 1960 (Zuercher Taschenbuch 80, pp. 11-28): pp. 15-16 report the decipherment of the first cipher from the passage 'hoc in ipsius fore preiudicium' and give its alphabet, null list and nomenclator (Tabellen I-III); pp. 20-21 print deciphered passages of the second cipher ('Nostris interim diligenter cavendum est ne quid precipitanter faciam ...') with translation, noting a few groups that 'trotzen einer sicheren Aufloesung'
prior_art.literature: P. Schweizer, Geschichte der Schweizerischen Neutralitaet (1895) pp. 233-236, cited by Usteri p. 14-15 as the first notice of the secret correspondence and of Frau von Peblis keeping the key

1244.key_check: Both keys are reconstructed and printed by Usteri (Tabellen I-III); not re-tested here because no leaf is online
1244.duplicates: known.py 'Breitinger' 'Peblis' 'E II 399': only this lead's own row and sweep
1244.closed: Printed decipherment and keys: Usteri, Zuercher Taschenbuch 80 (1960) pp. 15-22 solves both of Peblis's ciphers for exactly these folios of E II 399/400, prints the alphabet, nulls and nomenclator and deciphered passages, and states that Breitinger wrote the plaintext in the margin or on a separate sheet for most letters; only a few garbled groups are left unresolved.
